ledger.claim: The scheduled pickup was 07:30:00 and the record's own deadline is 07:35:00, five minutes later, yet the trip record reports arrived_by_deadline false and arrived_at null: the driver had not reached the pickup by that deadline. Under POL-NS-24 the rider may then cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full, so the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee on the fare ledger must be returned in full to the rider, which under POL-GEN-03 is FULL_REFUND of the whole contested amount with no driver compensation.

The driver-device trace is clean and complete - 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s, admissibility weight 1.0 - and it never corroborates arrival: the derived arrival check against the 50 m STANDARD-zone radius records corroborated false and nearest_fix null, and the trace ends with the driver stationary at 0 km/h from 07:33:10 all the way through the 07:37:40 cancellation. On POL-NS-21's arrival test the driver was not at the pickup, which is exactly the fact POL-NS-24's no-show refund rests on.

POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the driver's arrival, and on this record arrived_at is null, so no free wait ever began. A driver who never started a free wait cannot have had any no-show entitlement mature against a rider who was still waiting past 07:35.

POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait. Here the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED and no driver cancellation, and the fare ledger shows the 5.00 SGD charged to the rider with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. The clause that fixes the 5.00 SGD figure therefore does not authorise this charge, and the amount should be returned.

No traffic-data record was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING, carries issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact. The driver's 'jam at Sembawang Road' (EV-CHAT-05055, MSG-05055-001, repeated in the counterparty statement) is therefore uncorroborated, and POL-NS-24 gives the driver's arrival deadline no traffic exception in any event.

The rider does not press POL-NS-23: the record shows a driver message at 07:31:10 and an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so on this record the contact obligation was met. That concession does not rescue the fee, because POL-NS-24's refund turns on the missed arrival deadline, not on contact.

Nothing this ruling needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged and the case can be decided rather than held: the missed deadline is on the trip record, the driver's own chat at 07:36:30 says 'Still jam, sorry' - his own words confirming he was not at the pickup - and the trace never corroborates arrival. The absence of an arrival event here is a positive finding, not an unestablishable fact.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is fully satisfied, so the fee cannot be voided on that ground. The trip record's in-app call log shows a call placed by the driver at 07:33:20, answered and lasting 40 s; the chat log shows driver messages at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30. Both the message limb and the call limb were therefore in place before the 07:37:40 cancellation, and POL-NS-23's remedy — voiding the fee and refunding the rider in full — is not triggered. No FULL_REFUND can rest on the contact ground.

The amount charged is exactly the no-show fee the policy fixes, so there is nothing for a refund to correct. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD and total_charged of 5.00, and the derived money block confirms fee_matches_policy true against a policy_fee_sgd of 5.00 with refund_already_issued_sgd of 0.00. Where a no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes it the driver's compensation for the time and fuel already spent on the trip.

Even on POL-NS-24's own terms the rider's recovery is capped at the fee and no more. The clause adds a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact'; here the driver both messaged the rider (MSG-05055-001, read at 07:31:18) and placed an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, so the goodwill limb is not engaged and adds nothing to the rider's claim.

The cancellation is the rider's own act. The record's reason code is RIDER_CANCELLED, the rider's message at 07:35:00 gives her motive (she was 'going to be late for work'), and her own claim says she 'cancelled and booked another car'. The record shows a driver who was still en route and in contact with her throughout, so the filer's assertion that 'the driver was the one who was late' does not make out a case to disturb the present state, in which the charge stands and 0.00 has been refunded. Under POL-GEN-03 the correct outcome for a rider-filed dispute whose claim is not supported is NO_ACTION, which preserves that payment state.

If the case is not decided on the driver's contact compliance, the record does not settle the one fact that separates a driver stranded by the road from a driver who abandoned the booking. The GPS trace shows 2.448 km of continuous movement toward the pickup before the driver came to a halt at 07:33:10 and stayed stationary to the cancellation — consistent with the congestion he reported twice in the chat log (07:31:10 and 07:36:30). The only artifact that could test that explanation, the traffic advisory, is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 carries no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0 on the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, so the congestion can be neither confirmed nor refuted. Under POL-GEN-26 a fact the record cannot establish goes to a human reviewer, and on an escalation the fee is held rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the rider booked TRP-05055 for a 07:30 pickup and cancelled at 07:37:40. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05055) carries no arrival event at all — arrived_at is null and its own deadline check records arrived_by_deadline false against the 07:35:00 deadline (scheduled 07:30:00 plus the policy's 5 minutes) — and the driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s, weight 1.0) never places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone pickup radius: nearest_fix is null, corroborated is false, and the trace ends with the vehicle stationary, about 1.1 km short, at 0 km/h from 07:33:10 through the cancellation. POL-NS-24 therefore applies on its own test: the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, so the rider was entitled to cancel at no charge and the whole 5.00 SGD fee on the payments ledger (EV-FARE-05055, cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded. Ruling: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation. The driver's grounds are answered. POL-NS-23: the contact obligation was met (driver message MSG-05055-001 at 07:31:10 and an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation), and the rider concedes it — but POL-NS-23 only voids the fee for missing contact and cannot authorise a charge that fails POL-NS-24. POL-NS-22: the 5.00 SGD figure charged is exactly the policy fee, but that clause charges it only where the driver cancels after the free wait; here the rider cancelled (RIDER_CANCELLED) and the free wait never began, because POL-NS-21 runs it from the driver's arrival and arrived_at is null. POL-GEN-03 (NO_ACTION): declined, because the rider's claim is supported by the record. POL-GEN-26: declined, because the one artifact said to be missing (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, weight 0.0) carries no fact and nothing POL-NS-24 needs is unestablished — the missed deadline is decided on the trip record and the GPS trace, and POL-NS-24 gives the arrival deadline no traffic exception. The driver did attempt contact, so the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is not engaged, and no other referral fires: the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD (so POL-NS-22's amount check adds nothing) and the fee does not stand, so POL-NS-25's repeat count cannot reach three.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
